key_insight: Adding local electronic-structure and surface-environment features to WWL-GPR lets a graph-based model predict dopant-dependent adsorption and transition-state energies on ZrO2 surfaces more accurately than simple linear scaling rules.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more data-efficient way to screen doped oxide catalysts and better estimate downstream CH3OH yield trends without running DFT for every intermediate and transition state.
method: Represent adsorbate-surface structures as attributed graphs.
Train WWL-GPR with added oxide-relevant electronic and local-environment descriptors.
Benchmark against TSR for intermediates and BEP for transition states, then propagate predictions through microkinetic modeling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that WWL-GPR consistently improves intermediate energetics over scaling relations, yields competitive transition-state estimates versus BEP, and produces CH3OH yields closer to DFT-derived values after microkinetic propagation.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the quality and coverage of the training set, so extrapolation to new dopants, surfaces, or reaction conditions may be unreliable.
paper_title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
